    Finance Model API Reference¶

    newsegsmodelframework.newsegsfinance ¶

    Finance models: valuation of the output of a NewSEGS Energy Model.

    A finance model takes the results of a NewSEGS Energy Model and values them over a finance horizon. The base class and the discounting functions used by the finance and statistics code are exposed here; the implementation used by the Sprake model is in sprakefinance.

    Modules:

    Name Description
    common

    Discounting and aggregation functions shared by the finance models.
    newsegsfinance

    NewsegsFinance, the base class, and its data and configuration.
    sprakefinance

    SprakeFinance, the Sprake finance model.
    lightweightnewsegsfinance

    LightweightNewsegsFinance, a description of a finance model without the machinery to run it.

    Classes:

    Name Description
    NewsegsFinance

    Abstract base class of NewSEGS Finance model.

    Functions:

    Name Description
    apply_discount_factor

    Apply a discrete discount factor to a date-indexed DataFrame.
    sum_all_to_horizon

    Return the sum of all values up to a horizon.

    NewsegsFinance ¶

    Bases: NewsegsFinanceInterface

    Abstract base class of NewSEGS Finance model.

    Uses the results timeseries of a NewsegsModel instance in combination with configuration variables to calculate costs and benefits associated with energy generation, sales, and imports.

    Methods:

    Name Description
    run

    Perform any expensive computation required to "un-dirty" the finance
    set_model

    Attach the NewSEGS Energy Model whose results the finance model values.
    set_discount_rates

    Set the benefit and cost discount rates
    get_total_present_benefits_undiscounted

    The sum to horizon of undiscounted benefits.
    get_total_present_benefits_discounted

    The sum to horizon of discounted benefits.
    get_total_present_costs_undiscounted

    The sum to horizon of undiscounted costs.
    get_total_present_costs_discounted

    The sum to horizon of discounted costs.
    get_benefits_series_undiscounted

    All benefits collapsed to a single series indexed by datetime (without discount)
    get_benefits_series_discounted

    All benefits collapsed to a single series indexed by datetime (discounted)
    get_costs_series_undiscounted

    All costs collapsed to a single series indexed by datetime (without discount)
    get_costs_series_discounted

    All costs collapsed to a single series indexed by datetime (discounted)
    get_benefits_costs_undiscounted

    Undiscounted benefits and costs as the columns of a dataframe indexed by datetime.
    get_benefits_costs_discounted

    Discounted benefits and costs as the columns of a dataframe indexed by datetime.
    get_benefit_cost_ratio_undiscounted

    The ratio of undiscounted benefits to undiscounted costs up to the horizon.
    get_benefit_cost_ratio_discounted

    The ratio of discounted benefits to discounted costs up to the horizon.
    get_simple_payback_time_days

    The simple payback time in days.
    get_net_present_value_undiscounted

    The undiscounted net value to horizon: benefits less costs.
    get_net_present_value_discounted

    The net present value to horizon: discounted benefits less discounted costs.

    Attributes:

    Name Type Description
    finance_version str

    Version of the finance model.
    resident_receipts_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of resident receipts.
    resident_receipts_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of resident receipts (benefits discount applied).
    ev_receipts_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of EV receipts.
    ev_receipts_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of EV receipts (benefits discount applied).
    export_receipts_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of grid export receipts.
    export_receipts_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of grid export receipts (benefits discount applied).
    all_receipts_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of receipts.
    all_receipts_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of receipts (benefits discount applied).
    import_costs_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of grid import costs.
    import_costs_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of grid import costs (costs discount applied).
    om_costs_generation_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of o&m costs of generators.
    om_costs_generation_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of o&m costs of generators (cost discount applied).
    om_costs_storage_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of o&m costs of storage technologies.
    om_costs_storage_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of o&m costs of storage technologies (cost discount applied).
    om_costs_billing_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of billing costs.
    om_costs_billing_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of billing costs (cost discount applied).
    om_costs_other_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of other costs.
    om_costs_other_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of other costs (cost discount applied).
    all_recurrent_costs_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of recurrent costs.
    all_recurrent_costs_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of recurrent costs (cost discount applied).
    capex_costs_generation_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of capital expenditures for generation.
    capex_costs_generation_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of capital expenditures for generation (cost discount applied).
    capex_costs_storage_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of capital expenditures for storage.
    capex_costs_storage_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of capital expenditures for storage (cost discount applied).
    capex_costs_distribution_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of capital expenditure on distribution (undiscounted).
    capex_costs_distribution_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of capital expenditure on distribution (cost discount applied).
    capex_costs_metering_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of capital expenditure on metering (undiscounted).
    capex_costs_metering_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of capital expenditure on metering (cost discount applied).
    capex_costs_other_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of other capital expenditure (undiscounted).
    capex_costs_other_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of other capital expenditure (cost discount applied).
    all_capex_costs_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of all capital expenditure (undiscounted).
    all_capex_costs_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of all capital expenditure (cost discount applied).
    all_costs_undiscounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of all costs, recurrent and capital (the columns of the systems are suffixed _recurrent and _capex) (undiscounted).
    all_costs_discounted DataFrame

    Frame of timeseries of all costs, recurrent and capital (the columns of the systems are suffixed _recurrent and _capex) (cost discount applied).

    class NewsegsFinance(NewsegsFinanceInterface):
    """
    Abstract base class of NewSEGS Finance model.

    Uses the results timeseries of a NewsegsModel instance in combination with
    configuration variables to calculate costs and benefits associated with
    energy generation, sales, and imports.
    """

    _name = 'NewSEGS Finance Model'
    _finance_version = '0.0.1'
    _id_prefix = COMPONENT_PREFIXES['fm']

    _excluded_attributes = NewsegsFinanceInterface._excluded_attributes.union({'_model'})

    finance_data = ComponentProperty(default = NewsegsFinanceData)

    model = ComponentProperty(default = None)

    last_update: float = 0.0

    checked_out: bool = False

    def _generate_config(self, *args, **kwargs) -> DataWithRevision:
        return NewsegsFinanceConfig(*args, **kwargs)

    def __init__(
            self, 
            *args,
            model: Optional[newsegsmodelinterface.NewsegsModelInterface] = None,
            finance_data: Optional['NewsegsFinanceData'] = None,
            table_config: Optional['TableConfigNewsegsComponent'] = None,
            **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

        if model is not None:
            self.set_model(model)

        self.finance_data = finance_data or NewsegsFinanceData()
        self.table_config = table_config or TableConfigNewsegsComponent()

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `finance_version` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    @property
    def finance_version(self) -> str:
        """Version of the finance model.
        """
        return self.version

    def run(self):
        """
        Perform any expensive computation required to "un-dirty" the finance
        """
        super().run()
        return hash(self)

    # The model is assumed run, and used to extract results for providing the derived financial properties
    def set_model(
        self, 
        mdl: newsegsmodelinterface.NewsegsModelInterface,
        dirty: bool = True
    ) -> None:
        """Attach the NewSEGS Energy Model whose results the finance model values.

        Args:
            mdl: The NewSEGS Energy Model.
            dirty: Whether to mark the finance model as needing to be rerun.
        """
        last_revision = self.revision
        self.model = mdl
        if not dirty:
            self._config._revision = last_revision

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `set_discount_rates` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    def set_discount_rates(self, *drs:float, **kwdrs:float) -> None:
        """
        Set the benefit and cost discount rates

        Note that if only one positional argument is given, both discount rates
        will be set to this value.

        If mixing positional and keyword arguments, note that `benefit_discount_rate`
        is always the first positional argument, and will be over-written by a
        subsequent keyword argument of that key.

        Args:
            benefit_discount_rate: Also first positional argument (float)
            cost_discount_rate: Also second positional argument (float)
        """
        if len(drs) == 1 and len(kwdrs) == 0:
            # Assume that user wants to set both discount rates to nominated value
            dr = drs[0]
            self.benefit_discount_rate = dr
            self.cost_discount_rate = dr
        else:
            argnames = ['benefit_discount_rate', 'cost_discount_rate']
            argdict = dict(zip(argnames, drs))
            argdict.update(kwdrs)
            self.benefit_discount_rate = argdict.get('benefit_discount_rate', self._benefit_discount_rate) or 0.0
            self.cost_discount_rate = argdict.get('cost_discount_rate', self._cost_discount_rate) or 0.0

    # Benefits
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def resident_receipts_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of resident receipts.

        Broken down into `fixed_receipts`, `var_receipts`, `receipts` (i.e.
        total).
        """

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `resident_receipts_discounted` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def resident_receipts_discounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of resident receipts (benefits discount applied).

        Broken down into `fixed_receipts`, `var_receipts`, `receipts` (i.e.
        total).
        """

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def ev_receipts_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of EV receipts.

        Broken down into `fixed_receipts`, `var_receipts`, `receipts` (i.e.
        total).
        """

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `ev_receipts_discounted` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def ev_receipts_discounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of EV receipts (benefits discount applied).

        Broken down into `fixed_receipts`, `var_receipts`, `receipts` (i.e.
        total).
        """

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def export_receipts_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of grid export receipts.

        Broken down into `fixed_receipts`, `var_receipts`, `receipts` (i.e.
        total). In this instance, fixed_receipts may be used for capacity 
        payments.
        """

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `export_receipts_discounted` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.

        Broken down into `fixed_receipts`, `var_receipts`, `receipts` (i.e.
        total). In this instance, fixed_receipts may be used for capacity 
        payments.
        """

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def all_receipts_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of receipts.

        Columns are divided into a multi-index by `customer` and `receipt`.
        `customer` may be e.g. 'resident', 'ev', 'export' and `receipt`
        may be `fixed_receipts`, `var_receipts` and `receipts` (i.e. total).
        """

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def all_receipts_discounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of receipts (benefits discount applied).

        Columns are divided into a multi-index by `customer` and `receipt`.
        `customer` may be e.g. 'resident', 'ev', 'export' and `receipt`

        """

    @abstractmethod

        """
        The sum to horizon of undiscounted benefits.
        """

    @abstractmethod
    def get_total_present_benefits_discounted(self, horizon:pd.Timestamp|pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """
        The sum to horizon of discounted benefits.
        """

    @abstractmethod

        """The sum to horizon of undiscounted costs.

        The sum of all the costs up to the horizon, with no discount applied.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            Total costs.
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def get_total_present_costs_discounted(self, horizon:pd.Timestamp|pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """The sum to horizon of discounted costs.

        The sum of all the costs up to the horizon, with the cost discount applied.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            Total discounted costs.
        """
        ...

    # Summary vectors
    @abstractmethod
    def get_benefits_series_undiscounted(self) -> pd.Series:
        """
        All benefits collapsed to a single series indexed by datetime (without discount)
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def get_benefits_series_discounted(self) -> pd.Series:
        """
        All benefits collapsed to a single series indexed by datetime (discounted)
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def get_costs_series_undiscounted(self) -> pd.Series:
        """
        All costs collapsed to a single series indexed by datetime (without discount)
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def get_costs_series_discounted(self) -> pd.Series:
        """
        All costs collapsed to a single series indexed by datetime (discounted)
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def get_benefits_costs_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Undiscounted benefits and costs as the columns of a dataframe indexed by datetime.

        Returns:
            The dataframe with `benefits` and `costs` columns.
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def get_benefits_costs_discounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Discounted benefits and costs as the columns of a dataframe indexed by datetime.

        Returns:
            The dataframe with `benefits` and `costs` columns.
        """
        ...

    # Derived values
    @abstractmethod
    def get_benefit_cost_ratio_undiscounted(self, horizon:pd.Timestamp|pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """The ratio of undiscounted benefits to undiscounted costs up to the horizon.

        Where the costs are zero the ratio is infinite, signed as the benefits.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            The ratio.
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def get_benefit_cost_ratio_discounted(self, horizon:pd.Timestamp|pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """The ratio of discounted benefits to discounted costs up to the horizon.

        Where the costs are zero the ratio is infinite, signed as the benefits.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            The ratio.
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def get_simple_payback_time_days(self) -> float:
        """The simple payback time in days.

        The time from the start of the run until the cumulative undiscounted net revenue (receipts less recurrent costs) has repaid the capital expenditure. If this is not reached within the run it is extrapolated from the rate at which the debt is being reduced; it is infinite if the debt is not being reduced.

        Returns:
            The time in days.
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def get_net_present_value_undiscounted(self, horizon:pd.Timestamp|pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """The undiscounted net value to horizon: benefits less costs.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            The net value.
        """
        ...

    @abstractmethod
    def get_net_present_value_discounted(self, horizon:pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """The net present value to horizon: discounted benefits less discounted costs.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            The net present value.
        """
        ...

    def __hash__(self):
        mdl = self.model
        if mdl is None:
            return hash(
                (
                    self.id,
                    self.revision,
                )
            )
        return hash(
            (
                self.id,
                self.revision,
                mdl.id,
                mdl.last_run
            )
        )

    def set_model(
    self, 
    mdl: newsegsmodelinterface.NewsegsModelInterface,
    dirty: bool = True
) -> None:
    """Attach the NewSEGS Energy Model whose results the finance model values.

    Args:

    last_revision = self.revision

    def set_discount_rates(self, *drs:float, **kwdrs:float) -> None:
    """
    Set the benefit and cost discount rates

    Note that if only one positional argument is given, both discount rates
    will be set to this value.

    If mixing positional and keyword arguments, note that `benefit_discount_rate`
    is always the first positional argument, and will be over-written by a
    subsequent keyword argument of that key.

    Args:
        benefit_discount_rate: Also first positional argument (float)
        cost_discount_rate: Also second positional argument (float)
    """
    if len(drs) == 1 and len(kwdrs) == 0:
        # Assume that user wants to set both discount rates to nominated value
        dr = drs[0]
        self.benefit_discount_rate = dr
        self.cost_discount_rate = dr
    else:
        argnames = ['benefit_discount_rate', 'cost_discount_rate']
        argdict = dict(zip(argnames, drs))
        argdict.update(kwdrs)
        self.benefit_discount_rate = argdict.get('benefit_discount_rate', self._benefit_discount_rate) or 0.0
        self.cost_discount_rate = argdict.get('cost_discount_rate', self._cost_discount_rate) or 0.0

    def apply_discount_factor(
    undiscounted_df: pd.DataFrame, 
    discount_rate:float, 
    shift:int=0
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Apply a discrete discount factor to a date-indexed DataFrame.

    Args:
        undiscounted_df: DataFrame indexed by date, containing values to discount.
        discount_rate: Discount rate as a float.
        shift: Number of periods to shift the discount factors by.

    Returns:
        DataFrame with values discounted by the computed discount factors.
    """
    if len(undiscounted_df) == 0:
        return undiscounted_df 

    disc_factor = discount_factor_discrete(pd.Series(undiscounted_df.index), discount_rate)
    if shift != 0:
        disc_factor = disc_factor.shift(shift, fill_value=1.0) # Assuming shift will be +1 to account for end-of-interval accrued costs
    return undiscounted_df.apply(lambda col: col*disc_factor, axis=0)

    def sum_all_to_horizon(
    date_indexed_df: pd.DataFrame, 
    horizon: pd.Timestamp | pd.Timedelta | None = None
) -> float:
    """Return the sum of all values up to a horizon.

    Args:
        date_indexed_df: DataFrame indexed by date containing values to sum.
        horizon: Optional horizon as a Timestamp or Timedelta. If None, the last
            date in the index is used.

    Returns:
        The sum of all values in the DataFrame up to and including the horizon.
    """
    if horizon is None:
        horizon = date_indexed_df.index[-1]
    elif isinstance(horizon, pd.Timedelta):
        horizon = date_indexed_df.index[0] + horizon
    date_indexed_df = date_indexed_df.loc[date_indexed_df.index<=horizon, :]
    return date_indexed_df.sum().sum()

    Notes

    Discount factors are applied in discrete years (per https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4661216/#Sec9). A year is determined to have passed if the numeric year has increased and the day of year is >= the first day of the series. This implies that the calendar date of increment may vary depending on whether the present year is a leap year.

    def discount_factor_discrete(
        datetimes:pd.Series, 
        discount_rate:float
    ) -> pd.Series:
    """Return series of (left-aligned) discount factors for times in series.

    Args:
        datetimes: Series of datetimes.
        discount_rate: Discount rate as a float.

    Returns:
        Series of discount factors indexed by the input datetimes.

    Notes:
        Discount factors are applied in discrete years (per https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4661216/#Sec9).
        A year is determined to have passed if the numeric year has increased and the day of year is >= the first
        day of the series. This implies that the calendar date of increment may vary depending on whether the present
        year is a leap year.
    """
    idx = year_index(datetimes)

    return pd.Series(data = (1.0 + discount_rate)**(-idx), index=datetimes)

    class NewsegsFinance(NewsegsFinanceInterface):
    """
    Abstract base class of NewSEGS Finance model.

    Uses the results timeseries of a NewsegsModel instance in combination with
    configuration variables to calculate costs and benefits associated with
    energy generation, sales, and imports.
    """

    _name = 'NewSEGS Finance Model'
    _finance_version = '0.0.1'
    _id_prefix = COMPONENT_PREFIXES['fm']

    _excluded_attributes = NewsegsFinanceInterface._excluded_attributes.union({'_model'})

    finance_data = ComponentProperty(default = NewsegsFinanceData)

    model = ComponentProperty(default = None)

    last_update: float = 0.0

    checked_out: bool = False

    def _generate_config(self, *args, **kwargs) -> DataWithRevision:
        return NewsegsFinanceConfig(*args, **kwargs)

    def __init__(
            self, 
            *args,
            model: Optional[newsegsmodelinterface.NewsegsModelInterface] = None,
            finance_data: Optional['NewsegsFinanceData'] = None,
            table_config: Optional['TableConfigNewsegsComponent'] = None,
            **kwargs):
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

        if model is not None:
            self.set_model(model)

        self.finance_data = finance_data or NewsegsFinanceData()
        self.table_config = table_config or TableConfigNewsegsComponent()

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `finance_version` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    @property
    def finance_version(self) -> str:
        """Version of the finance model.
        """
        return self.version

    def run(self):
        """
        Perform any expensive computation required to "un-dirty" the finance
        """
        super().run()
        return hash(self)

    # The model is assumed run, and used to extract results for providing the derived financial properties
    def set_model(
        self, 
        mdl: newsegsmodelinterface.NewsegsModelInterface,
        dirty: bool = True
    ) -> None:
        """Attach the NewSEGS Energy Model whose results the finance model values.

        Args:
            mdl: The NewSEGS Energy Model.
            dirty: Whether to mark the finance model as needing to be rerun.
        """
        last_revision = self.revision
        self.model = mdl
        if not dirty:
            self._config._revision = last_revision

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `set_discount_rates` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    def set_discount_rates(self, *drs:float, **kwdrs:float) -> None:
        """
        Set the benefit and cost discount rates

        Note that if only one positional argument is given, both discount rates
        will be set to this value.

        If mixing positional and keyword arguments, note that `benefit_discount_rate`
        is always the first positional argument, and will be over-written by a
        subsequent keyword argument of that key.

        Args:
            benefit_discount_rate: Also first positional argument (float)
            cost_discount_rate: Also second positional argument (float)
        """
        if len(drs) == 1 and len(kwdrs) == 0:
            # Assume that user wants to set both discount rates to nominated value
            dr = drs[0]
            self.benefit_discount_rate = dr
            self.cost_discount_rate = dr
        else:
            argnames = ['benefit_discount_rate', 'cost_discount_rate']
            argdict = dict(zip(argnames, drs))
            argdict.update(kwdrs)
            self.benefit_discount_rate = argdict.get('benefit_discount_rate', self._benefit_discount_rate) or 0.0
            self.cost_discount_rate = argdict.get('cost_discount_rate', self._cost_discount_rate) or 0.0

    # Benefits
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def resident_receipts_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of resident receipts.

        Broken down into `fixed_receipts`, `var_receipts`, `receipts` (i.e.
        total).
        """

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `resident_receipts_discounted` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def resident_receipts_discounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of resident receipts (benefits discount applied).

        Broken down into `fixed_receipts`, `var_receipts`, `receipts` (i.e.
        total).
        """

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def ev_receipts_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of EV receipts.

        Broken down into `fixed_receipts`, `var_receipts`, `receipts` (i.e.
        total).
        """

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `ev_receipts_discounted` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def ev_receipts_discounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of EV receipts (benefits discount applied).

        Broken down into `fixed_receipts`, `var_receipts`, `receipts` (i.e.
        total).
        """

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def export_receipts_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of grid export receipts.

        Broken down into `fixed_receipts`, `var_receipts`, `receipts` (i.e.
        total). In this instance, fixed_receipts may be used for capacity 
        payments.
        """

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `export_receipts_discounted` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.

        Frame of timeseries of grid export receipts (benefits discount applied).

        Broken down into `fixed_receipts`, `var_receipts`, `receipts` (i.e.
        total). In this instance, fixed_receipts may be used for capacity 
        payments.
        """

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def all_receipts_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of receipts.

        Columns are divided into a multi-index by `customer` and `receipt`.
        `customer` may be e.g. 'resident', 'ev', 'export' and `receipt`
        may be `fixed_receipts`, `var_receipts` and `receipts` (i.e. total).
        """

    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def all_receipts_discounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of receipts (benefits discount applied).

        Columns are divided into a multi-index by `customer` and `receipt`.
        `customer` may be e.g. 'resident', 'ev', 'export' and `receipt`

        """

        """

        """

        """

        The time from the start of the run until the cumulative undiscounted net revenue (receipts less recurrent costs) has repaid the capital expenditure. If this is not reached within the run it is extrapolated from the rate at which the debt is being reduced; it is infinite if the debt is not being reduced.

        Returns:
            The time in days.
        """

    def get_net_present_value_discounted(self, horizon:pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """The net present value to horizon: discounted benefits less discounted costs.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            The net present value.
        """
        ...

    def __hash__(self):
        mdl = self.model
        if mdl is None:
            return hash(
                (
                    self.id,
                    self.revision,
                )
            )
        return hash(
            (
                self.id,
                self.revision,
                mdl.id,
                mdl.last_run
            )
        )

    def set_model(
    self, 
    mdl: newsegsmodelinterface.NewsegsModelInterface,
    dirty: bool = True
) -> None:
    """Attach the NewSEGS Energy Model whose results the finance model values.

    Args:
        mdl: The NewSEGS Energy Model.
        dirty: Whether to mark the finance model as needing to be rerun.
    """
    last_revision = self.revision
    self.model = mdl
    if not dirty:
        self._config._revision = last_revision

    def set_discount_rates(self, *drs:float, **kwdrs:float) -> None:
    """
    Set the benefit and cost discount rates

    Note that if only one positional argument is given, both discount rates
    will be set to this value.

    If mixing positional and keyword arguments, note that `benefit_discount_rate`
    is always the first positional argument, and will be over-written by a
    subsequent keyword argument of that key.

    Args:
        benefit_discount_rate: Also first positional argument (float)
        cost_discount_rate: Also second positional argument (float)
    """
    if len(drs) == 1 and len(kwdrs) == 0:
        # Assume that user wants to set both discount rates to nominated value
        dr = drs[0]
        self.benefit_discount_rate = dr
        self.cost_discount_rate = dr
    else:
        argnames = ['benefit_discount_rate', 'cost_discount_rate']
        argdict = dict(zip(argnames, drs))
        argdict.update(kwdrs)
        self.benefit_discount_rate = argdict.get('benefit_discount_rate', self._benefit_discount_rate) or 0.0
        self.cost_discount_rate = argdict.get('cost_discount_rate', self._cost_discount_rate) or 0.0

If this is not reached within the run it is extrapolated from the rate at which the debt is being reduced; it is infinite if the debt is not being reduced.

    Returns:
        The time in days.
    """

    """Configuration of the Sprake finance model: the discount rates and the unit costs.

    Attributes:
        wind_capex_per_kw: Capital cost of wind generation (per kW).
        wind_om_per_kw_year: Annual operating and maintenance cost of wind generation (per kW).

        grid_import_var_per_unit: Price of electricity imported from the grid (per kWh).

    class SprakeFinance(newsegsfinance.NewsegsFinance):
    """Implementation of NewsegsFinance for Sprake Model."""
    _name = 'Sprake Finance Model'

    _meter_names = {
        'resident_consumption': ('appliance_import', 'dhw_import', 'spaceheat_import'),
        'ev_consumption': ('evcharge_import'),
        'grid_export': ('grid_export'),

        'grid_import': ('grid_import')
    }

    def _generate_config(self, *args, **kwargs) -> newsegsfinance.DataWithRevision:
        return SprakeFinanceConfig(*args, **kwargs)

    @singledispatchmethod
    def __init__(
        self,
        dispatch_arg: Mapping | float|int | SprakeFinance,
        *args,
        **kwargs,
    ) -> None:
        raise ValueError('First argument must be a Mapping, a Number, or a SprakeFinance, is %s', type(dispatch_arg))

    # Copy constructor is registered underneath class definition for late-bind

    @__init__.register(float|int)
    def _from_number(
        self,
        benefit_discount_rate: float|int,
        *args,
        horizon: int = -1,
        **kwargs
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            *args,
            benefit_discount_rate = benefit_discount_rate,
            **kwargs
        )

        self.horizon = horizon

    @__init__.register(dict)
    def _from_dict(
        self,
        unit_costs: Mapping,
        *args,
        horizon: int = -1,
        **kwargs
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)

        self.set_unit_costs_from_dict(unit_costs)
        self.horizon = horizon

    @classmethod
    def from_none(cls):
        """Create a Sprake finance model with default values.

        Returns:
            The finance model.
        """
        return cls(0.0)

    def set_unit_costs_from_dict(self, input_dict: Mapping) -> None:
        """
        Update all unit costs using a dictionary.

        Check `SprakeFinance.get_default_unit_costs()` for expected values
        """
        for k, v in input_dict.items():
            if not hasattr(SprakeFinanceConfig, k):
                raise AttributeError(f'Unit cost not known: {k}; Available values are {list(SprakeFinanceConfig.__dict__.keys())}')

            setattr(self, k, v)

    @override
    def set_model(
        self, 
        mdl: NewsegsModelInterface,
        dirty: bool = True
    ) -> None:
        if not isinstance(mdl, SprakeModel):
            raise TypeError(f'SprakeFinance only compatible with SprakeModel, {type(mdl)} provided')
        return super().set_model(mdl, dirty)

    @override
    def run(self):
        self.last_update = time.time_ns()
        return super().run()

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `get_default_unit_costs` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    @classmethod
    def get_default_unit_costs(cls) -> dict:
        """
        Return the default unit cost dictionary
        """
        odict = asdict(_DEFAULT_UNIT_COSTS)
        _clean_unit_cost_dict(odict)
        return odict

    @property
    def unit_costs(self) -> dict:
        """
        Get a copy of the current unit cost dictionary
        """
        odict = asdict(self._config) # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]
        _clean_unit_cost_dict(odict)
        return odict

    def _get_empty_df(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return _deferred_get_empty_df(self).copy()

    def _get_consumption(self, meter_names) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Summarise consumption meters to a simple dataframe
        """
        return _deferred_get_consumption(self, meter_names).copy()

    def _get_resident_consumption(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return self._get_consumption(self._meter_names['resident_consumption'])

    def _get_ev_consumption(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return self._get_consumption(self._meter_names['ev_consumption'])

    def _get_grid_export(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return self._get_consumption(self._meter_names['grid_export'])

    def _get_grid_import(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        return self._get_consumption(self._meter_names['grid_import'])

    # Benefits
    @property
    def resident_receipts_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Frame of timeseries of receipts from residents (undiscounted). Calculated from the results of the NewSEGS Energy Model.
        """
        return _deferred_get_resident_receipts_undiscounted(self).copy()

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `resident_receipts_discounted` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    @property
    def resident_receipts_discounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Frame of timeseries of receipts from residents (benefit discount applied). Calculated from the results of the NewSEGS Energy Model.
        """
        return _deferred_get_resident_receipts_discounted(self).copy()

    @property
    def ev_receipts_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Frame of timeseries of receipts from EV charging (undiscounted). Calculated from the results of the NewSEGS Energy Model.
        """
        return _deferred_get_ev_receipts_undiscounted(self).copy()

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `ev_receipts_discounted` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    @property
    def ev_receipts_discounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Frame of timeseries of receipts from EV charging (benefit discount applied). Calculated from the results of the NewSEGS Energy Model.
        """
        return _deferred_get_ev_receipts_discounted(self).copy()

    @property
    def export_receipts_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Frame of timeseries of receipts for electricity exported to the grid (undiscounted). Calculated from the results of the NewSEGS Energy Model.
        """
        return _deferred_get_export_receipts_undiscounted(self).copy()

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `export_receipts_discounted` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    @property
    def export_receipts_discounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Frame of timeseries of receipts for electricity exported to the grid (benefit discount applied). Calculated from the results of the NewSEGS Energy Model.
        """
        return _deferred_get_export_receipts_discounted(self).copy()

    @property
    def all_receipts_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Frame of timeseries of all receipts (the benefits) (undiscounted).
        """
        return _deferred_get_all_receipts_undiscounted(self).copy()

    @property
    def all_receipts_discounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Frame of timeseries of all receipts (the benefits) (benefit discount applied).
        """
        return _deferred_get_all_receipts_discounted(self).copy()

    def get_total_present_benefits_undiscounted(self, horizon:pd.Timestamp|pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """The sum to horizon of undiscounted benefits.

        The sum of all the benefits (receipts) up to the horizon, with no discount applied.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            Total benefits.
        """
        return _deferred_get_total_present_benefits_undiscounted(
            self,
            horizon
        )

    def get_total_present_benefits_discounted(self, horizon:pd.Timestamp|pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """The sum to horizon of discounted benefits.

        The sum of all the benefits (receipts) up to the horizon, with the benefit discount applied.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            Total discounted benefits.
        """
        return _deferred_get_total_present_benefits_discounted(self, horizon)

    # Costs

    @property
    def import_costs_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Frame of timeseries of costs of electricity imported from the grid (undiscounted). Calculated from the results of the NewSEGS Energy Model.
        """
        return _deferred_get_import_costs_undiscounted(self).copy()

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `import_costs_discounted` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    @property
    def import_costs_discounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Frame of timeseries of costs of electricity imported from the grid (cost discount applied). Calculated from the results of the NewSEGS Energy Model.
        """
        return _deferred_get_import_costs_discounted(self).copy()

    @property
    def om_costs_generation_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """
        Frame of timeseries of o&m costs of generators.

        Broken down into `wind_costs`, `pv_costs` and `costs` (i.e. total).
        O&M costs are accrued in single monthly payments.
        """
        return _deferred_get_om_costs_generation_undiscounted(self).copy()

    # REVIEW (unreferenced): no references to `om_costs_generation_discounted` found in src/, scripts/ or data/.
    @property
    def om_costs_generation_discounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """

    def get_total_present_costs_undiscounted(self, horizon:pd.Timestamp|pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """The sum to horizon of undiscounted costs.

        The sum of all the costs up to the horizon, with no discount applied.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            Total costs.
        """
        return _deferred_get_total_present_costs_undiscounted(self)

    def get_total_present_costs_discounted(self, horizon:pd.Timestamp|pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """The sum to horizon of discounted costs.

        The sum of all the costs up to the horizon, with the cost discount applied.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            Total discounted costs.
        """
        return _deferred_get_total_present_costs_discounted(self)

    # Summary vectors
    def get_benefits_series_undiscounted(self) -> pd.Series:
        """All benefits collapsed to a single series indexed by datetime (without discount).

        Returns:
            The series, named `benefits`.
        """
        return _deferred_get_benefits_series_undiscounted(self).copy()

    def get_benefits_series_discounted(self) -> pd.Series:
        """All benefits collapsed to a single series indexed by datetime (discounted).

        Returns:
            The series, named `benefits`.
        """
        return _deferred_get_benefits_series_discounted(self).copy()

    def get_costs_series_undiscounted(self) -> pd.Series:
        """All costs collapsed to a single series indexed by datetime (without discount).

        Returns:
            The series, named `costs`.
        """
        return _deferred_get_costs_series_undiscounted(self).copy()

    def get_costs_series_discounted(self) -> pd.Series:
        """All costs collapsed to a single series indexed by datetime (discounted).

        Returns:
            The series, named `costs`.
        """
        return _deferred_get_costs_series_discounted(self).copy()

    def get_benefits_costs_undiscounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Undiscounted benefits and costs as the columns of a dataframe indexed by datetime.

        Returns:
            The dataframe with `benefits` and `costs` columns.
        """
        return _deferred_get_benefits_costs_undiscounted(self).copy()

    def get_benefits_costs_discounted(self) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Discounted benefits and costs as the columns of a dataframe indexed by datetime.

        Returns:
            The dataframe with `benefits` and `costs` columns.
        """
        return _deferred_get_benefits_costs_discounted(self).copy()

    # Derived values
    def get_benefit_cost_ratio_undiscounted(self,  horizon:pd.Timestamp|pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """The ratio of undiscounted benefits to undiscounted costs up to the horizon.

        Where the costs are zero the ratio is infinite, signed as the benefits.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            The ratio.
        """
        return _deferred_get_benefit_cost_ratio_undiscounted(self)

    def get_benefit_cost_ratio_discounted(self,  horizon:pd.Timestamp|pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """The ratio of discounted benefits to discounted costs up to the horizon.

        Where the costs are zero the ratio is infinite, signed as the benefits.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            The ratio.
        """
        return _deferred_get_benefit_cost_ratio_discounted(self)

    def get_simple_payback_time_days(self) -> float:
        """The simple payback time in days.

        The time from the start of the run until the cumulative undiscounted net revenue (receipts less recurrent costs) has repaid the capital expenditure. If this is not reached within the run it is extrapolated from the rate at which the debt is being reduced; it is infinite if the debt is not being reduced.

        Returns:
            The time in days.
        """
        return _deferred_get_simple_payback_time_days(self)

    def get_net_present_value_undiscounted(self, horizon:pd.Timestamp|pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """The undiscounted net value to horizon: benefits less costs.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            The net value.
        """
        return _deferred_get_net_present_value_undiscounted(self, horizon)

    def get_net_present_value_discounted(self, horizon:pd.Timestamp|pd.Timedelta|None=None) -> float:
        """The net present value to horizon: discounted benefits less discounted costs.

        Args:
            horizon: Time up to which to sum, as a timestamp or a timedelta from the start of the data; the end of the data if None.

        Returns:
            The net present value.
        """
        return _deferred_get_net_present_value_discounted(self, horizon)

    def set_unit_costs_from_dict(self, input_dict: Mapping) -> None:
    """
    Update all unit costs using a dictionary.

    Check `SprakeFinance.get_default_unit_costs()` for expected values
    """
    for k, v in input_dict.items():
        if not hasattr(SprakeFinanceConfig, k):
            raise AttributeError(f'Unit cost not known: {k}; Available values are {list(SprakeFinanceConfig.__dict__.keys())}')

        setattr(self, k, v)

    @classmethod
def get_default_unit_costs(cls) -> dict:
    """
    Return the default unit cost dictionary
    """
    odict = asdict(_DEFAULT_UNIT_COSTS)
    _clean_unit_cost_dict(odict)
    return odict

    get_simple_payback_time_days() ¶

    The simple payback time in days.

    The time from the start of the run until the cumulative undiscounted net revenue (receipts less recurrent costs) has repaid the capital expenditure. If this is not reached within the run it is extrapolated from the rate at which the debt is being reduced; it is infinite if the debt is not being reduced.

    Returns:

    Type Description
    float

    The time in days.
